title: Introducing AI Translations: Your Docs in Every Language
summary: Your developers read your docs in their own language while your team keeps writing in one. AI Translations covers every page and re-translates a page whenever it changes.
body_markdown:
Today we're launching[AI Translations](https://docs.readme.com/ent/docs/language-support-and-localization) . Turn on a language and AI translates every page of your docs across every project you pick. When a page changes, its translation changes with it. Your developers read your docs in their language, and your team keeps writing in yours.

## Docs Your Developers Can Read


Developers everywhere build on APIs documented in English, but most of them would rather read a guide in their own language. Translated docs used to mean hiring a vendor, sending them a second set of files, waiting for their response. The translations fell behind as soon as the English docs changed.


Now you pick a language, pick the projects, and click **Turn On** . Every page is translated, and readers pick their language from your docs. From then on, every commit to a page re-translates it, so a translated page is never older than the page it came from.

## Create an API key


Every request is signed with a secret key from your dashboard.


## One Switch, Every Page


AI Translations covers every page, all at once: guides, API reference, changelog, and reusable content. It reads the same ReadMe markdown your writers use, so callouts, code samples, tables, and embeds are unchanged. Your code samples and product names stay exactly how you want them.


Each language has one page in the group dashboard that shows where it stands: which projects it covers, when each was last translated, and whether anything needs a look. Need another language? Ask, and your Customer Success Manager unlocks it.


## Your Voice, in Every Language


Good translations keep your tone and branding. If you give the AI context for a language, like a formal register for German or the product names that stay in English, every page it translates follows. Terms that should never be translated go on a list, and they stay as written in every language and every project.


If a page needs sign-off before it goes live, turn on **Review Before Publishing** . Translations then wait on a review branch until someone on your team merges them, just like the rest of your doc changes.

## Get Started


AI Translations are available today on Enterprise plans.


To translate your docs:


1. Open the **Group Dashboard** and go to **AI Translations** . If your language isn't unlocked yet, ask your Customer Success Manager.
2. Pick the language, choose which projects get it, and click **Turn On** .
3. Add context for the AI and the terms to keep, and decide whether translations go live right away or wait for review.


The[localization guide](https://docs.readme.com/ent/docs/language-support-and-localization) covers what gets translated, how re-translation works, and the languages we support. Don't have Enterprise?[Talk to us](https://readme.com/enterprise) about translating your docs.
